question: Who among the following was one of the finest calligraphers at Akbar's court, who was honoured with the title 'Zarrin Qalam' (golden pen)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Muhammad Husayn**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Muhammad Husayn was one of the most distinguished calligraphers during the reign of Emperor Akbar.
 
• He was honoured with the title 'Zarrin Qalam' which means 'golden pen'.
 
• His work was highly regarded and he played a significant role in the cultural and artistic development of Akbar's court.
 
• Muhammad Husayn’s calligraphy was notable for its elegance and precision, earning him a place of high esteem among his contemporaries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calligraphy**

 
 
• Calligraphy is a visual art related to writing. It is the design and execution of lettering with a broad-tipped instrument, brush, or other writing instruments.
 
• In the context of Islamic art, calligraphy is a highly venerated form of artistic expression, often used to transcribe verses from the Quran.
 
 
 
• **Akbar's Court**
 
 
• Akbar the Great (1556-1605) was the third Mughal Emperor who is known for his cultural and administrative achievements.
 
• His court was a hub of artistic and intellectual activities, attracting talents from various fields including literature, music, painting, and calligraphy.
 
• Akbar's patronage played a crucial role in the development of Mughal art and culture.
 
 
 
• **Abul Fazal**
 
 
• Abul Fazal was a historian and one of the nine jewels (Navaratnas) of Akbar's court.
 
• He authored the Akbarnama, the official history of Akbar's reign in three volumes.
 
 
 
• **Daswant and Basawan**
 
 
• Daswant and Basawan were prominent painters at Akbar's court known for their contributions to the Mughal school of painting.
 
• They were instrumental in the development of the miniature painting style that characterized Mughal art.
